drivingQuestion: Which declarations of purpose invalidate the slaughter of a non-sacred animal?
outcomeNote: A mishna: the first tanna's list and closing principle stand, with R' Shimon's dissent recorded and undecided.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַשּׁוֹחֵט לְשֵׁם עוֹלָה, לְשֵׁם זְבָחִים, לְשֵׁם אָשָׁם תָּלוּי, לְשֵׁם פֶּסַח, לְשֵׁם תּוֹדָה – שְׁחִיטָתוֹ פְּסוּלָה, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַכְשִׁיר.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» In the case of «one who slaughters» an animal and asserts that he is slaughtering it «for the sake of a burnt offering, for the sake of a peace offering, for the sake of a provisional guilt offering, for the sake of a Paschal offering,» or «for the sake of a thanks offering, his slaughter is not valid,» as it appears that he is consecrating animals and slaughtering sacrificial animals outside the Temple. «And Rabbi Shimon deems» his slaughter «valid.»

segments.he: שְׁנַיִם אוֹחֲזִין בְּסַכִּין וְשׁוֹחֲטִין, אֶחָד לְשׁוּם אֶחָד מִכׇּל אֵלּוּ, וְאֶחָד לְשׁוּם דָּבָר כָּשֵׁר – שְׁחִיטָתוֹ פְּסוּלָה. הַשּׁוֹחֵט לְשֵׁם חַטָּאת, לְשֵׁם אָשָׁם וַדַּאי, לְשֵׁם בְּכוֹר, לְשֵׁם מַעֲשֵׂר, לְשֵׁם תְּמוּרָה – שְׁחִיטָתוֹ כְּשֵׁרָה.
segments.en: If there were «two» people «grasping a knife» together «and slaughtering» an animal, «one» slaughtering «for the sake of one of all those» enumerated in the first clause of the mishna «and one» slaughtering «for the sake of a legitimate matter,» their «slaughter is not valid.» With regard to «one who slaughters» an animal «for the sake of a sin offering, for the sake of a guilt offering» for «a definite» transgression, «for the sake of» the offering of «a firstborn, for the sake of» the offering of animal «tithe,» or «for the sake of a substitute» for a sacrificial animal, «his slaughter is valid.» All of these offerings may be brought only as obligations and not as gifts. Therefore, there is no concern that he consecrated the animals.

segments.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁנִּידָּר וְנִידָּב – הַשּׁוֹחֵט לִשְׁמוֹ אָסוּר, וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ נִידָּר וְנִידָּב – הַשּׁוֹחֵט לִשְׁמוֹ כָּשֵׁר.
segments.en: «This is the principle:» For «any item,» i.e., offering, «which» is consecrated as a voluntary «vow or gift,» in the case of «one who slaughters for its sake» the animal is «forbidden. And» for any offering «that is not» consecrated as a voluntary «vow or gift» but is an obligation that is incumbent upon him, in the case of «one who slaughters for its sake» the animal is «permitted.»

moves.summary: one who slaughters for the sake of a burnt, peace, provisional guilt, Paschal or thanks offering — his slaughter is invalid
moves.about: whether declaring that one slaughters a non-sacred animal for the sake of an offering that may be vowed or donated invalidates the slaughter

moves.summary: R' Shimon deems the slaughter valid
if two hold the knife, one slaughtering for a disqualifying purpose and one for a valid one, the slaughter is invalid
slaughtering for the sake of a sin offering, definite guilt offering, firstborn, tithe or substitute is valid, since these come only as obligations
the governing principle: anything that can be vowed or donated disqualifies, anything that cannot does not
